chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If an impoverished man is enabled to perform hajj by another man, he will have a hajj. But if he later becomes financially able, then hajj is still obligatory upon him. Likewise, the nāṣib, if he comes to know, then hajj is obligatory upon him, even if he had already performed hajj.

key_terms.أَحَجَّهُ: caused him or enabled him to perform hajj
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: one who bears enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ: a performed hajj counted for him
key_terms.عَرَفَ: came to know or recognize the truth

ai.seo_question: Does hajj remain obligatory if someone performed it while poor or before recognizing the truth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on hajj for one who performed it without full financial ability through another person’s support. It also states that if a nāṣib comes to recognize the truth, hajj becomes obligatory upon him even if he had previously performed it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2867 - Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"If an impoverished man is sent for Hajj by another person, it will count as a Hajj for him. However, if he later becomes financially capable, Hajj will still be obligatory upon him. Similarly, a Nasibi (one who opposes the Ahlulbayt), if he comes to recognize the truth, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him, even if he had already performed it previously."
